header: Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 PT | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE) — Evan Torres (CISO, Auriga), Maya Patel (Cloud Architect), Liam O'Neal (DevOps)
summary: Discovery focused on Auriga's security requirements for evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Main concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and least privilege, audit logging/retention, encryption/KMS key management, and data residency/retention policies. Redwood to share SOC2 report, schedule deep technical session and provide a PoC runbook for on-prem/dedicated testing.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 compliance
SSO / SAML / SCIM and enterprise SSO flows
RBAC, tenant isolation and least privilege
Audit logs, retention windows, and forensic access
Encryption at rest/in transit, KMS / HSM integration
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Data residency and retention policies for PHI/PCI workloads
PoC plan: latency benchmarks, KV cache, and model version pinning
transcript: [00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time — quick intros?

[00:08] Evan (Auriga CISO): Evan Torres here, I'm the CISO. Maya's our cloud architect, Liam runs infra. Main ask today: security posture — SOC2, encryption, SSO — we want to understand risk before we go further.
[00:22] Jordan: Perfect. Priya and Samir from our SE team will cover technicals; my role is commercial and to make sure we answer compliance questions.

[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi, quick agenda: compliance artifacts we can share, SSO/SAML and SCIM support, RBAC model, audit logs / retention, KMS options, and deployment choices (hosted, dedicated, private).

[00:45] Maya (Cloud Architect): Great. To start: are we looking at hosted API or private? Auriga likely needs dedicated or private for regulated data — PHI in some pipelines — but we need to understand isolation and key control.

[01:02] Samir (Redwood SE): Totally. Hosted is our fastest onboarding model; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and stronger isolation; Private lets you run a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem. For PHI, many customers pick Dedicated with KMS integration or Private if they require customer-managed HSMs.
[01:25] Liam (DevOps): For Private, do we get full access to logs and the audit trail? We need to plug into our SIEM and retain logs for 1 year minimum.

[01:36] Priya: Yes — with Private you control the control plane and logs. We support streaming audit logs to S3/CloudWatch and can push to your SIEM via an integration. Retention windows are configurable; default hosted retention is 90 days but Dedicated/Private can be extended per contract.
[01:55] Evan: Can you share SOC 2 evidence? We have an infosec questionnaire and our audit team will want controls mapped.
[02:02] Jordan: We'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and our ISO summary after the call; I'll drop links. Also we have a security questionnaire PDF and an internal controls mapping doc we can send.
[02:15] Maya: On SSO — we use Okta with SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. We need SSO for RBAC and want to ensure session expiry and automated user deprovisioning.

[02:25] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. Sessions can be configured with session timeouts, and we can integrate with your IdP for SCIM user sync to enforce deprovisioning. There's a minor caveat with hosted tokens for API keys — we can rotate keys programmatically and tie API keys to a user or service principal.
[02:45] Liam: What about least privilege? Can you create roles scoped to model endpoints and per-team quotas?

[02:52] Samir: Our RBAC supports role templates (viewer, dev, infra, admin) and you can create custom roles scoped to specific routes/models and to per-project billing. On Dedicated/Private, you can enforce stricter network policies as well.

[03:06] Evan: Audit logs — what granularity? We need logs of all request metadata, configs changes, key rotations, and model rollouts for compliance. Also ability to prove who accessed specific transcripts or prompt history.

[03:17] Priya: Logs include request metadata (timestamp, route, user or service principal, model id, latency, status), control plane events (deploys, rollouts, config changes), and auth events. For sensitive content we offer redaction options and can limit transcript storage — you can opt out of storing prompts on-hosted if required.
[03:35] Maya: Encryption — at rest and in transit. KMS integration with customer-managed keys? HSM support?

[03:42] Samir: We encrypt in transit (TLS 1.2+), and at rest with AES-256. For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed keys via BYOK flows. Hosted can use our managed KMS but we support CMKs on Dedicated with contract clauses.
[03:58] Evan: Data residency — some workloads can't leave EU. Does Redwood offer region locking or deploy to customer-specified regions?

[04:05] Priya: Yes, we offer region-specific deployments. Hosted has region options, Dedicated reservations can be provisioned in specific cloud regions, and Private can be deployed into customer VPC in a selected region. We also have controls for logs and backups residency.
[04:22] Liam: About model caching / KV cache — are cached prefixes stored? We need to ensure any cached content doesn't persist beyond retention windows or leak across tenants.

[04:31] Samir: KV cache and prefix caching are tenant-scoped; we do not share caches across tenants. Retention is configurable and for sensitive data customers often disable persistent caching or set aggressive eviction. We'll include cache controls in the PoC runbook.
[04:48] Maya: For a PoC, we'd like to validate latency under load for our typical seq lengths (1k tokens) and test prompt redaction. Can Redwood run a benchmark inside our VPC?

[04:58] Priya: Yes — for Dedicated we can run benchmark instances; for Private we can provide an on-prem deployment package and a runbook. We'll propose a plan: 1) test harness in your VPC, 2) KV cache configs, 3) model pinning to specific quantized variants and measure tail latencies.
[05:14] Evan: Compliance docs: will you provide architecture diagrams, network flows, and a list of sub-processors?
[05:20] Jordan: Yes, we'll send a security pack: SOC2 report, ISO summary, architecture/flow diagrams, list of subprocessors, and our data processing addendum for review.
[05:30] Liam: On contract, is there an option for dedicated physical tenancy? We prefer strong isolation for PHI workloads.

[05:37] Samir: Dedicated is logically isolated VMs/GPU pools with tenant isolation and encrypted storage; we can discuss physical isolation in enterprise agreements if needed — that's typically part of Private/on-prem options.
[05:49] Maya: What about incident response and breach notification SLAs? We need 24h first response and detailed forensics within 72h.

[05:57] Priya: Our incident response policy includes 24h acknowledgement and a forensics timeline; we'll include the playbook and escalation contacts in the packet. For Dedicated/Private customers we can add tighter contractual SLAs.
[06:10] Evan: Are there known gaps? Anything we should be aware of that might affect our security review?

[06:16] Jordan: We try to be transparent — hosted default retention is 90 days which some enterprises consider low; we can extend retention for Dedicated/Private. Also hosted uses our managed KMS by default — if customer-managed keys are a hard requirement, Dedicated/Private is the path.
[06:30] Liam: SCIM provisioning — can we auto-provision service accounts with limited scopes?
[06:35] Samir: Yes, service principals can be provisioned via SCIM and bound to custom roles. We also support short-lived API credentials and token rotation.
[06:46] Maya: For audit purposes can we export a full immutable audit trail for a given timeframe?
[06:51] Priya: Exports are possible; we can stream to your S3 with MFA delete or to your SIEM. For Private you have full control over log retention and immutability policies.
[07:03] Evan: On cryptography, does Redwood support FIPS-140 validated modules where required?
[07:09] Samir: We use cloud provider crypto stacks which can be FIPS-compliant; if FIPS is required we'll surface the exact configuration as part of the security pack and discuss HSM options.
[07:22] Maya: Any limitations on throughput for Dedicated — expected per-GPU throughput and autoscaling behavior?

[07:29] Priya: Dedicated offers reserved capacity with autoscaling policies and burst options; we'll include expected throughput numbers for common model families in the runbook. We can also do a sizing session based on your qps and token distribution.
[07:45] Evan: We will send over our security questionnaire. Can you map controls to our questions and identify any gaps quickly?
[07:51] Jordan: Yes, once you send the questionnaire we'll map items to SOC2 controls and Redwood policies and highlight gaps. We'll also flag items that require contract amendments.
[08:03] Maya: Timeline — we are aiming to choose a vendor in 4–6 weeks and start a pilot in the following month. That ok?
[08:09] Jordan: That timeline works. Next steps: I'll send the SOC2 and security pack; Priya will schedule a technical deep dive; Samir will kick off a PoC plan draft. Any final Qs?
[08:20] Liam: One small item: do you persist full request/response pairs for embeddings and can that be disabled?
[08:27] Samir: By default we store embeddings metadata and hashed references; raw text storage can be disabled or redacted. We'll include the exact flags in the doc.
[08:38] Evan: Good. Thanks all — we'll wait for the pack and tech invite.
[08:44] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the deep dive. Meeting ends.
[58:00] End of recording
